features.name: title_has_emotional_or_personal_identifier
features.definition: Does the title contain an explicit emotional expression or explicit personal identifier (e.g., first-person self-reference or stated personal identity)?
features.spec: Read only the title. Return 1 if the title explicitly contains an emotional word/expression (e.g., hate, love, afraid, angry, feel) or an explicit personal identifier (first-person self-reference such as I/my/me, or a stated personal identity/attribute of the author such as 'as a woman', 'I'm a veteran'). Return 0 otherwise. Ignore the 'CMV:' prefix. Do not count impersonal topic words alone. Do not count view-change or delta announcements. Missing title gives null.

h0: title_has_emotional_or_personal_identifier is not associated with the likelihood of the OP changing their view.
h1: Posts with title_has_emotional_or_personal_identifier = 1 have a lower likelihood of the OP changing their view than those with 0.
note: Operational assumption: "explicit emotional or personal identifiers" is interpreted as explicit emotion words or first-person/personal identity markers in the title; the hypothesis does not define them precisely. Association only. Titles may be edited and could contain outcome text, though unlikely.
